misconceptions.description: Treating the capstone plan as a folder that staples together each module piece rather than a coherent plan where the parts reinforce one objective
misconceptions.trigger: candidate submits scenario, prompts, adaptations, and noticing as disconnected sections with no through-line
misconceptions.feedback: Show how each module move serves one teaching goal. A coherent plan is integrated, not collated.

misconceptions.description: Letting TeachGen@i generate the whole capstone plan and presenting it as the candidate's professional judgment
misconceptions.trigger: the plan shows no teacher edits, no rejected suggestions, and no decisions the candidate can defend as their own
misconceptions.feedback: The plan must record where you accepted, edited, and rejected AI input. Undocumented AI authorship is not your judgment.

misconceptions.description: Making the plan's competing demands disappear instead of naming the tradeoff and defending the choice
misconceptions.trigger: candidate hides a tension such as coverage vs. depth rather than stating which they chose and why
misconceptions.feedback: Surface each tradeoff and defend the call. A plan that pretends there were no hard choices is not yet professional.
